title: Smart scan hedging and multi-key prefetch probe for dashboard query API
creator: Alyssa Chen
description: Problem: Long-tail tail-latency on certain dashboard queries (filters + multi-join aggregates) is causing occasional user-visible stalls and higher p99s. Existing prefix caching and single-key prefetch reduce median latency but under multi-key fanout queries we see repeated disk/remote fetches and amplified stalls. Goal: Validate whether a lightweight hedging strategy combined with a multi-key prefetch probe (small speculative multi-key read issued early in the request lifecycle) can reduce p95/p99 without increasing average cost significantly. This ticket scopes an experiment that implements a non-invasive probe layer in the Console query API that: 1) detects multi-key fanout patterns; 2) issues a small, bounded prefetch probe for the top N keys (configurable) concurrently with the query planner; 3) performs single-request hedging when a backend shard does not respond within a short SLO; 4) records detailed telemetry for cost/latency/benefit analysis. The probe must be opt-in per-tenant and toggleable via the Console feature flags. We will evaluate both synthetic replay and sampling in production (1% of queries) before any rollout.
acceptance_criteria: - Implementation compiles and passed unit tests and integration test harnesses for query planner.
acceptance_criteria_2: - Feature flagging exists and can enable the probe per-tenant with rollout percent control.
acceptance_criteria_3: - Synthetic replay shows >= 30% reduction in p99 for identified query shapes with <10% token/IO cost increase in the probe path.
acceptance_criteria_4: - Production 1% sample run for 48 hours demonstrates p95/p99 improvements with telemetry collected and annotated. No regressions in other query types.
tasks: Design probe: define key-selection heuristic and bounding (Alyssa)
Add feature-flag + per-tenant toggle to Console config (Diego)
Implement speculative multi-key prefetch probe in query gateway with bounded concurrency (Eng team)
Implement lightweight hedging: second request to alternate replica after hedging-threshold (Eng team)
Add telemetry spans and cost tagging (tracing, token/IO counters)
Create synthetic replay harness and baseline dataset (SRE/Bench)
Run 1% production sampling, analyze results, and prepare rollout recommendation
notes: Design trade-offs: cheerful balance between cost and latency. Probe must be small (N <= 8) and capped bytes to avoid amplification.
We should avoid double-counting cache hits; probe reads should be recorded with cost tags separate from normal path.
If hedging fires, ensure we record which replica responded first; use that to weight routing heuristics later.
Consider adding adaptive N selection based on tenant QPS and historic fanout distribution in a follow-up.
Keep API surface unchanged for callers; all speculation is internal to the gateway/runtime.
